Sports.title: Injury crisis and a transfer embargo... welcome to life as a manager, Aaron Ramsey! Former Arsenal star excited for new start as Oxford United boss
Sports.content:
Injury crisis and a transfer embargo... welcome to life as a manager, Aaron Ramsey! Former Arsenal star excited for new start as Oxford United boss

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aaron Ramsey was barely a fortnight into his first managerial role when Oxford United confirmed they had been placed under a transfer embargo for failing to comply with the EFL's new salary rules.

Welcome to the new job, Aaron. You simply can't absorb that sort of rug-pulled-from-under-feet sensation by reading the manuals or attending coaching workshops.

A few days later, Frankie Kent, a centre-half signed on a free from Hearts and the only summer recruit Oxford made before the transfer ban hit, damaged cruciate knee ligaments in training and underwent an operation that will rule him out for most of the season.

Ramsey could have been excused for checking the small print in the contract.

'Absolutely not,' he said at a press briefing on Friday, as he confirmed more injury setbacks with left back Ruben Roosken and South Korea international striker Jeon Jin-woo both ruled out for two to three months. 'We're fully committed, me and my staff. We came here to work with these players and our focus is on them.'

Ramsey says he has not spoken to Mikel Arteta, his friend and former Arsenal teammate, since taking the Oxford job, although they share a similar manner in front of the cameras.

Aaron Ramsey is looking forward to his first managerial role at Oxford United despite the club being placed under a transfer embargo just weeks after his appointment

Oxford have also seen their preparations for the new season hit by a series of injuries

Like Arteta, Ramsey is perfectly polite and yet guarded and brisk. He moves quickly through the room to his seat with a flurry of handshakes, fields the questions without giving much away, smiles, says thanks and disappears with even greater speed.

Perhaps this is the survival mode for modern managers. It hasn't done Arteta any harm.

Ramsey has worked out his own protection techniques having spent 20 of his 35 years amid the glare of expectation.

He was a wonderkid who made his Cardiff debut at 16. He had played in an FA Cup final, joined Arsenal and won his first Wales cap before he was 18.

He was still only 19 when his career was almost ended by a horrific leg break, an impact so painful he revealed this week that he dislocated his jaw screaming.

Ramsey will always have a metal rod in his right leg as a reminder of that day in Stoke, but his recovery and success at Arsenal, winning the FA Cup three times and scoring the winner in the final twice, and 86 international caps, helping Wales reach the last four of Euro 2016, testify to his quiet determination.

'I'm immensely proud of what I achieved, especially since what I had to overcome,' said Ramsey. 'You don't always get the fairytale endings you want but if I look back at my career that's been a fairytale in itself.'

Seven years since leaving Arsenal, however, have been disjointed. A lucrative move to Juventus brought more medals but few plaudits and as he moved into his 30s, he became increasingly plagued by muscle injuries he suspects can probably be traced back to the broken leg.

Ramsey won three FA Cups during his time at Arsenal after recovering from horrific leg break he suffered at 19, which led to him having a metal rod inserted into his right leg

His former team-mate and current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had encouraged Ramsey to take his coaching badges early, helping him build towards a career in management

Ramsey had two years back at hometown club Cardiff, which ended with him injured and taking caretaker charge for three matches as they were relegated to League One

A loan to Rangers will be defined by his missed penalty in the shootout of the Europa League final. There was a season in France with Nice, two years back at Cardiff which ended with him injured and in caretaker charge of his hometown club for the last three games as they were relegated to League One.

THREE TIES TO WATCH THIS WEEKEND West Ham v Portsmouth Nine thousand Pompey fans are expected to make the trip to their first game at West Ham since a 4-3 defeat at Upton Park nearly 15 years ago. It could be a record first round crowd for the Carabao Cup with much attention trained on the directors’ box however with David Sullivan expected to attend the game. Sullivan still owns a 38.8 per cent stake in West Ham but stepped down as co-chair in June after historical allegations of sexual misconduct were aired as part of a BBC Panorama investigation. He denies the allegations. Mansfield v Sheffield United Mansfield humbled the Blades in the FA Cup in January. Nigel Clough’s League One team were 4-1 up inside an hour at Bramall Lane. They resisted a fightback to win 4-3, then knocked out Premier League Burnley out before giving champions-to-be Arsenal a scare in the Fifth Round. Can the Stags do it again? Salford v Shrewsbury Salford City will be a little less Manchester United and a little more Dundee United this season after finally relenting to pressure from supporters to revert to their original orange-and-black home colours, 12 years after the Class of 92 takeover changed the colours to red.

And last season in Mexico where he suffered the ordeal of losing his beloved dog Halo from the family ranch before his decision to retire in March.

Little wonder he is relishing this new direction with the chance to sink his teeth into coaching challenges.

'It's something I've been building up to for a few years off the field,' said Ramsey. 'I had a conversation with Arteta when we were playing. He did his coaching badges towards the end of his career and said he wished he'd done it earlier because he started to see the game differently.

'So, it was important for me to take that advice at the time and do my badges in the last years of my career, which I did. And I'm grateful for opportunities I've had to coach in and out at Cardiff U18s in an unofficial role and in and around the Wales camp with Craig Bellamy allowing me to gain experience.

'That confirmed to me the direction I wanted to take. I'm more than ready for this.

'I think one of my strengths as a player was that I didn't get too high or too low. I'm fairly level, consistent in what I want to do and how I handle emotions. I'm calm but confident.'

After four wins in four pre-season friendlies, Oxford's season starts with a Carabao Cup tie at Leyton Orient before a League One opener at home to Milton Keynes Dons.

'I'm very excited to get stuck into the season,' said Ramsey, despite the complications.

Oxford expect to be compliant with the new salary rules and out of the embargo by January at the latest and the new boss swears there is no way he will be tempted to pull his boots on again. Not even if injuries continue to bite.

'Absolutely not,' said Ramsey. 'No, my playing days are firmly finished.'

Sports.title: Two viral sensations have joined South American giants, an Argentina villain now at Chelsea and the Aussie teenager set for a record move - how breakout stars are making the most of their World Cup fame
Sports.content:
Older football fans were wistful heading into the World Cup by suggesting the tournament no longer surprises us with players that people have been previously unaware of.

Gone were the days when an unheralded or young player would emerge from seemingly nowhere, leading to some of the world's biggest clubs falling over themselves in the hope of signing them.

With matches and data so accessible now, it was felt that clubs merely use the World Cup now as confirmation on what they already know about players. It is certainly the case with several of the transfers to have taken place post tournament, with clubs moving for targets they had targeted prior to the World Cup.

Yet the case of Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has appealed to the romantics, with the veteran landing a move directly off the back of his performances in the United States.

On Sunday, fans of Chilean giants Colo-Colo swarmed around the Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport to greet Vozinha, with their World Cup star having landed to complete a transfer.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at some of the post-World Cup deals with tournament stars looking to make an impact for new clubs following their impressive showings in North America.

World Cup cult hero Vozinha landed a move to Chilean side Colo-Colo following the tournament

Colo Colo fans waited outside the airport in Santiago on Sunday to welcome the goalkeeper

Vozinha

The 40-year-old goalkeeper finally sealed his post-World Cup move to Colo-Colo on Sunday after touching down in Santiago.

'I'm very happy to be here. And I want to thank the fans for the patience they've shown while waiting for me,' the Cape Verde star told reporters in Chile.

'See you at the Monumental Stadium.'

It completes a fairytale couple of months for the goalkeeper, who was one of the heroes of Cape Verde's surprise run to the last-32, before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

His standout performances were among the highlights of Cape Verde's debut appearance at the World Cup.

At the start of the Spain match in Cape Verde's World Cup opener, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram, but after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 28.6million followers.

Vozinha was named in FIFA's team of the tournament to complete a remarkable rise.

His move to Colo-Colo is the most high-profile of his career, after playing for clubs in his homeland, Moldova, Slovakia, Cyprus and Portugal's second tier.

Vozinha will now look to help Colo-Colo win the league title during his six-month contract, which includes an option of a 12-month extension.

Vozinha was catapulted to fame after his performances against Spain and Argentina

Ismael Saibari

Bayern Munich were keen to stress that their £43million signing of Morocco star Saibari had been part of their long-term planning, rather than a reaction to his World Cup displays.

'We're delighted to have secured the services of Ismael Saibari, one of the most exciting forwards at the World Cup,' said Max Eberl, FC Bayern board member for sport, when Saibari's move was made official on July 1.

'Transfers like this don't happen on the spur of the moment but are the result of long-term planning: the key factor was that we made our position clear to him early on because we were aware of Ismael's skills and were able to show him a clear future with us from the start.

'Ismael Saibari will bring extra quality and unpredictability to our attacking play.'

Saibari had led the line for Morocco at the World Cup, with the versatile attacker scoring in all three of their group stage matches.

He was forced off injured in their last-16 win over Canada, resulting in the 25-year-old having to watch from the stands as Morocco lost to France in the quarter-finals.

Saibari had come into the tournament off the back of being named as the Player of the Year in the Eredivisie, having helped PSV Eindhoven secure a third consecutive title.

The Moroccan has now reported to training with Bayern and will be looking to make an impact in the Bundesliga.

Bayern Munich completed the signing of Moroccan World Cup star Ismael Saibari for £43m

Bayern were keen to stress that Saibari was part of their long-term planning, rather than a reaction to his impressive World Cup displays

Valentin Barco

Chelsea's signing of Barco was confirmed after the World Cup, but was agreed long before it.

Daily Mail Sport reported back in May that the Blues had agreed to sign the former Brighton full back from their sister club Strasbourg – a 13th deal between the two BlueCo clubs.

Barco, who had been playing as a midfielder in Ligue 1, had earned a call-up to Argentina's World Cup squad off the back of his performances last season.

The 22-year-old had limited involvement for Argentina on their path to the World Cup final, featuring for just 19 minutes in a group stage match against Jordan.

That still did not stop Barco making an impact on the pitch, with the Argentina hitting the headlines when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove. Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

The reception Barco receives from English crowds this season will be interesting, while Chelsea fans will be hoping he can make an impact on the field of play.

Chelsea confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco's provocative celebrations irked England's Jude Bellingham after their semi-final clash

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

Johan Manzambi

'I am very, very happy and I am excited to play with this club,' Manzambi said after sealing his move from Freiburg to Aston Villa.

'It's a very big club in England, and they're playing in the Champions League. I've already played against Aston Villa, and for me, it was the perfect plan.

'I hope I can play the same as in the World Cup and with Freiburg.

'I'm sure that with the team, the coach and the staff that I can do the same.'

Manzambi opted for the move to Villa Park over Newcastle, despite the Magpies having a £49million bid accepted and had verbal agreement on terms with the 20-year-old.

The Swiss international had been one of the breakout stars of the World Cup, having initially begun the tournament as an impact substitute before forcing his way into a starting role.

Manzambi scored three goals and provided two assists until his tournament was cruelly ended by a knee injury.

While Manzambi played higher up the pitch for Switzerland, Aston Villa highlighted how he operated in a more deep-lying role for Freiburg. The midfielder had impressed Aston Villa during their preparations for the Europa League Final, even though Freiburg were beaten 3-0 by Unai Emery’s side in May.

Manzambi will be a central player in Aston Villa's revamped team this summer, with Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans having left the club and Amadou Onana out for a prolonged period with a knee injury.

Johan Manzambi began the World Cup on the bench before becoming a breakout star

The Swiss midfielder, who snubbed Newcastle, will be a key part of Aston Villa's new look midfield

Tim Payne

Like Vozinha, Payne was catapulted to fame at the World Cup where the New Zealander became a viral sensation.

Argentine content creator called Valen Scarsini, known as 'El Scarso', set out to find a player at the 48-team tournament in the US, Mexico and Canada who was unheralded and unknown for most fans.

He then wanted to see just how far his mission to make the player famous could go.

Payne ended up being his pick because the Wellington Phoenix centre-back only had 5,000 followers on Instagram.

Scarsini's bizarre campaign led to Payne's follower count exploding, with the 32-year-old now boasting over 5.6million followers.

The interest of a South American audience to Payne and New Zealand's World Cup campaign carried on, with the defender landing himself a transfer as a result.

Club Olimpia, Paraguay's biggest club, signed Payne ahead of the All Whites' first match of the tournament, reportedly paying £430,000 to Wellington Phoenix for his signature.

'Club Olimpia is one of the biggest clubs in South America, with an incredible history, passionate supporters and ambitions that match its stature, and I am looking forward to rising to that challenge,' Payne said when confirming his move.

'For our family, this is something really special. My son, growing up speaking Spanish like his mum did, immersing ourselves in her culture and her family's world is what makes this so much more than just a football move.'

Payne had also made the point of thanking Scarsini and his followers for their role in his life-changing move.

Payne made his debut for Olimpia on Sunday and marked it with a goal, curling a superb effort into the top corner from the edge of the box.

New Zealand's Tim Payne became a viral sensation after an Argentina influencer encouraged fans to follow him on Instagram, taking his followers from 5,000 to over 5.4million

⚽️¡QUÉ GOLAZO! Tim Payne debutó con la camiseta franjeada y en pocos minutos marcó este golazo.



📺Tigo Sports



▶️Viví el #ClausuraAPF2026 en https://t.co/pGNhXoLRh7 pic.twitter.com/zmObqWdI5i — Tigo Sports (@TigoSportsPY) August 2, 2026

Payne secured a move to Paraguyan side Olimpia after his profile was raised and marked his debut for the club with a superb goal on Sunday

Lucas Herrington

Herrington saw his World Cup end in heartbreaking fashion after sending a penalty over the crossbar in Australia's shootout defeat by Egypt in the last-32.

The 18-year-old was quickly offered support by Sweden great Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who praised his courage in stepping up to take the penalty at such a young age.

'Penalty is like lottery. You score, you become a hero, you don't score, sadly you become zero,' Ibrahimovic said.

'I just want to reach out to Herrington. You're 18 years old, you're young, this is just the beginning of your career.

'You stepping up there, you showed a lot of courage, not everybody will do that. My friend, you're the best. Don't listen to the rest. Listen, Herrington, if you want to reach out, I'm here.'

Exactly one month on and Herrington is closing in on a move from Colorado Rapids to the Premier League, with the teenager set to become the most expensive Australian player in history at around £17million.

Lucas Herrington suffered heartbreak after missing his penalty in Australia's shootout loss to Egypt

The teenage Australian defender is now expected to complete a move to Hull City

Herrington, who earned praise for his composed performances at the World Cup, is expected to seal a move to newly promoted Hull City, with their owner Acun Ilicali confirming their interest to the BBC on Saturday.

Asked if Herrington was someone Hull were looking at, Ilicali said: 'Yes.

'He's (got) very big potential. Very young boy. I think (a) future star. We are very close, very close.'

Asked when he thought a decision might be made on Herrington, Ilicali said: 'One week.'

Sports.title: Top football executive linked with replacing Gianni Infantino reports FIFA president to Ethics Committee - following failed plan to sell the World Cup, overturning of Florian Balogun's suspension and award of Peace Prize to President Trump
Sports.content:
Norwegian FA president Lise Klaveness will report Gianni Infantino to FIFA's Ethics Committee as European football intensifies pressure on the FIFA president.

UEFA have already pledged to boycott FIFA tournaments so long as Infantino remains FIFA president.

And the head of the Norwegian FA, Klaveness - who has been mooted as a potential successor to Infantino - endorsed that position after their monthly board meeting. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter is among those advocating for Klaveness to succeed Infantino.

The 45-year-old former lawyer will also submit a complaint to the FIFA Ethics Committee, which has the power to impose bans from football.

The complaint will not only challenge the proposed sale of a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors, but also the decision to award an ad hoc FIFA Peace Prize to President Donald Trump and the suspension of Florian Balogun's red card at the World Cup following alleged political pressure from Trump.

‘The board believes that we do not have confidence in Gianni Infantino. We did not have that in the last election and we do not have it now,’ Klaveness said.

‘There is no going back for Gianni Infantino. The international football community is very divided, and we must unite now.

Lise Klaveness has long been an opponent of Gianni Infantino

Klaveness spoke to reporters on Friday to explain the decisions taken at the Norwegian FA's monthly board meeting

Europe have upped the pressure on Infantino, with UEFA vowing to boycott FIFA competitions so long as he remains in post

‘We will ask the FIFA president to resign now. There is no doubt about it: there is a deep crisis in international football cooperation.

‘Irreversible transgressions have occurred,’ she added on the decision to complain to the ethics committee.

‘We have reached a situation where extraordinary measures are needed to create lasting change.’

UEFA are leading the charge to dethrone Infantino as FIFA president. However, the Swiss football administrator appears to retain support from Africa, South America and Asia - which is enough to fend off any leadership challenge.

Meanwhile, Mexico have broken ranks from CONCACAF's opposition to Infantino, reaffirming their confidence in the FIFA leadership.

UEFA's current refusal to play in FIFA competitions will cause the governing body significant commercial problems, potentially prompting Infantino to reconsider his position at the top of world football.

But the FIFA president has shown no sign of relenting thus far after being supported by the governing body's hierarchy on Wednesday.

Sports.title: 'Number one priority' - Amy Hunt makes intentions clear ahead of home European Athletics Championships
Sports.content:
'Number one priority' - Amy Hunt makes intentions clear ahead of home European Athletics Championships

The sprint sensation claimed Commonwealth Games silver over 100m and is now looking to make her mark in Birmingham

View Image Amy Hunt. (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Amy Hunt has made a promise to the fans in Birmingham this summer – they will be seeing plenty of her at the European Athletics Championships.

‌



The World Championship silver medallist over 200m has made the Europeans her absolute priority this summer and will compete over both 100m and 200m individually, as well as in two relays at the Alexander Stadium.

‌



That makes for a packed schedule, but Hunt would not have it any other way, in her first chance to compete at a major outdoor championship on home soil.

‌



She explained: “One of the great things about being a versatile sprinter is that I can compete over both the 100m and 200m. The downside is there are lots of opportunities, so sometimes it's difficult to say no.

“Our number one priority is the European Championships. It's the first time they've been held in the UK, so we're aiming to compete in the full programme there: the 100m, 200m, women's 4x100m and the new mixed 4x100m, because that would be really iconic.

“I'll be doing everything, so you'll probably be seeing a lot of me every day.”

‌



The mixed 4x100m relay will be particularly interesting, as it makes its major championships debut at the Alexander Stadium.

Hunt has shown her value as a relay runner in taking Olympic silver two years ago, a matter of weeks after a European gold, both in the women’s 4x100m.

And while sprinting is a very individual sport, Hunt relishes the opportunity to join forces with the likes of Dina Asher-Smith and Daryll Neita to bring back medals.

‌



She said: “That's one of the beautiful things about relays. Everyone brings different strengths, and together you create something even stronger.

“We know Great Britain has one of the best relay squads in the world, and we've consistently won medals on the biggest stages.

“We had relay practice and it was lovely seeing everyone again because we all live in different countries, so we don't get together very often. We caught up, talked about the season.

‌



“It might seem strange to people that we go from being rivals to teammates, but ultimately we all want to win. When we come together, we become even stronger.”

That catch-up with her relay colleagues came just before the Wanda Diamond League event at the London Stadium, where Hunt ran in the 4x100m relay and the 200m.

She was part of a British that won the relay, before having to settle for fifth in a high-class field in the 200m, won by Julien Alfred, the Olympic champion over 100m.

‌



Hunt produced a season’s best of 22.30, a hundredth faster than she had managed at the same event the year before.

She kicked on from that performance to produce the best showing of her career so far when she won World Championship silver in Tokyo last September.

And with her participation in London only confirmed in the days before because of an illness in the build-up that had forced her to cut short a training session, Hunt believes the signs are positive that she could come away with even more individual success this summer.

‌



She added: “It's pretty much the same time I ran here last year, so if anyone's paying attention, they'll know that's a pretty good omen.

“At Christmas I wrote down my goals, and now I'm starting to think, "Wow, maybe we can chase those." I think I'm always a bit of a dark horse going into championships, so no matter what's happened during my season, people should never write me off. I'm excited.”

As a former junior standout – Hunt still holds the world under-18 record for the 200m – this development to the highest level has not come as a complete surprise.

‌



She has achieved it while also studying at the University of Cambridge, from which she graduated in 2023, recovering from a ruptured tendon the previous year, before heading out to Padua, where she now trains.

That has meant putting education on the backburner while she focuses all her attention on athletics, but it remains something she is keen to explore.

She added: “I've always said I'd like to do a master's degree at some point.

‌



“That hasn't happened yet, partly because I now live in a country where I'm still not fluent in the language. But I'd definitely like to return to academia one day because I really enjoy it.

“I'm a human being before I'm an athlete. I want to experience the world, keep learning, grow intellectually, and be inspired by things outside my own little sporting bubble.

I think it's healthy to live as broad a life as possible.

‌



“There was a master's programme at the V&A that I was looking at recently, so perhaps that's something I'll come back to.

“Athletes, particularly women, are increasingly showing that our lives can be much broader than just track. We can study, have careers alongside athletics, and pursue different interests. Life is much bigger than the nine lanes out there.”

Life is bigger than those nine lanes, but when it comes to Birmingham, most of Hunt’s time will be spent racing down them.

Sports.title: Five Brits ready to shine at European Athletics Championships in Birmingham
Sports.content:
Five Brits ready to shine at European Athletics Championships in Birmingham

The likes of Keely Hodgkinson and Zharnel Hughes may hog the headlines but this quintet will hope to show what they can do on the big stage.

View Image Zharnel Hughes (centre). (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

The likes of Keely Hodgkinson and Zharnel Hughes will grab the headlines, but the European Athletics Championships also offer up-and-coming athletes the chance to shine.

‌



After all, it was on the European stage that Hodgkinson claimed her first senior outdoor gold medal – the 800m crown in Munich four years ago – while Dina Asher-Smith did the same back in 2016 in Amsterdam.

‌



So, for the packed-out crowds expected at Birmingham’s Alexander Stadium, this summer’s championship represents the chance to revel not only in the best of British athletics but also get a sneak peek at the sport’s future in this country. And to ensure that you are clued up on that next generation, we have picked out five emerging talents ready to spread their wings.

‌



Five to watch

Emily Newnham (400m hurdles and 400m)

Emily Newnham insists that her priority is the 400m hurdles, although given her form over 400m this season, she clearly has the potential excel in both events.

The 22-year-old from Shaftesbury Barnet has beaten her personal best both in the hurdles and the flat this year, building on a hugely promising 2025.

‌



She won a pair of medals at the European Indoors in the 4x400m relays before dominant displays at the European U23 Athletics Championships in Bergen saw her come away with two gold medals.

One of those came in the 400m hurdles, where she set a new championship record to finish more than a second clear of the field.

And with Dutch star Femke Broeders-Bol having made the step up to the 800m this season, Newnham will be hoping to take advantage of her absence at the head of the field.

‌



Newnham’s personal best of 53.92, set in Madrid this year, would have been enough for silver in this event two years ago, behind only Broeders-Bol, so she could be right in the mix this time around.

Success Eduan (200m)

Given her first name, Success Eduan had no choice but to flourish once she set her mind to athletics and she has certainly lived up to it so far in her career.

‌



The 21-year-old demonstrated her potential when she won a European U20 medal over 200m at just 17, and last year she claimed the European U23 title in style in Bergen over the same distance.

She also led home a British victory in the 4x100m at the World Relays Championships in 2025 but the moment which made everyone sit up and take notice came in 2026.

In the UK Champs in Birmingham, Eduan beat World Championship silver medallist to take the national title by more than two tenths and cement her place as one of the brightest sprinting prospects in the country.

‌



She is now set to return to the Alexander Stadium for more of the same against the continent’s best.

Kimani Jack (high jump)

The most unlikely name on this list is Kimani Jack, who has emerged from nowhere in 2026.

‌



A history graduate from the University of Birmingham, Jack won a pair of BUCS outdoor high jump titles and competed at the European U23s last year in Bergen.

But it is this year where he has really caught the eye, clearing 2.30m for the first time, with a personal best of 2.31m at the Torrin Lawrence Memorial in Athens, Georgia.

He followed that up by taking second on his Diamond League debut in Monaco, clearing 2.30m, and if he can manage that again in Birmingham, he should be right in the hunt for the podium.

‌



Charlotte Henrich (400m)

At just 19 years of age, Charlotte Henrich has already set two Welsh national records over 400m, beating a mark that had previously stood for 44 years.

Henrich ran 50.58 to finish third in the UK Championships in Birmingham, before lowering that record with a run of 50.45 seconds at the Wanda Diamond League in London.

‌



Those performances have singled Henrich out as a huge talent and while she might need to drop a couple more tenths to get into the battle for the medals, she has already shown a penchant for breaking records this season.

Innes FitzGerald (5000m)

Still only 20 years old, Innes FitzGerald has already got major championship experience under her belt after making her World Championship debut in Tokyo last September.

‌



While she did not progress through the heats there, FitzGerald will be a strong candidate to do so in Birmingham when she races over 5000m.

As a cross-country athlete, FitzGerald already has six European U20s titles, winning individual and team gold in each of the last three years, while in Tampere last summer she won 3000m and 5000m gold at the European U20 Championships by huge distances, breaking Gabriela Szabo’s 32-year-old championship record in the former.

She will not be able to run away from the competition in Birmingham, so tactical nous maybe an advantage for her more seasoned rivals, but in terms of potential, the sky is the limit for FitzGerald.

Sports.title: I shelved retirement plans for 'make or break' year - now I'm ready to take on Europe
Sports.content:
I shelved retirement plans for 'make or break' year - now I'm ready to take on Europe

Sam Bennett has come through injury hell and earned silver at the Commonwealth Games ahead of his home European Athletics Championships

View Image Sam Bennett celebrates his 110m hurdles silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Hurdler Sam Bennett has shelved retirement plans and is ready to take the European Athletics Championships by storm.

‌



Late last year, the 25-year-old from Southend suffered a torn posterior cruciate ligament, the latest in a line of injuries stretching back seven years. But at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, he surged back through the field behind Jamaican Damario Prince to take 110m hurdles silver and now has his eyes on more success in Birmingham.

‌



He said: “This year was make or break for me. It's a reinforcement of my own beliefs because everybody else might not have the same belief that I can make those performances. It’s like a checkbox next to my name that says, okay, he can perform when it matters.

‌



“It definitely does feel different. I think that it's been years of working towards that, and that's been a goal of mine for such a long time - having that reassurance that I am who I think I am and I can achieve what I truly thought I could, when everything on the track was telling me that I couldn't.

“I entered every single competition and wanted to win. That's the biggest thing that's been different for me this year. In previous years, I lost that. I lost the ability to win."

Bennett won the European U18 Championships and Commonwealth Youth Games before his injury troubles. He then headed stateside for six years, studying economics and psychology at Harvard and an economics Master’s at Howard’s. And after his hurdling stalled, he began to apply for corporate partnership roles.

‌



He said: “I always say that I graduated with 5,900 people and about 150 of them could have a conversation. I couldn’t do another year of watching the people who I've worked just as hard as to be in those positions travelling the world and competing for their country.

“It felt like I had the world in my hands and my momentum was going to continue in that way. Whether it was sponsors or money, I felt like I was about to get to that tipping point of where things were going to continue to snowball. And then obviously, in the last eight, nine years, I haven't even had a sniff at those things.

“Being within the U.S. collegiate system, I had the support of those people, but then coming out of that meant that being an independent and unsponsored athlete is pretty difficult and it's all on your back.”

Article continues below

But Bennett’s decision to throw everything at 2026 has paid dividends, as he beat his PB at the UK Athletics Championships in June before his Commonwealth exploits. Now, he forms part of a 98-strong Novuna GB & NI team seeking glory on home turf at the Alexander Stadium.

He said: “Having a home games is so special. I've never had anybody shout for me, for England, like they did at the Commonwealths. So now that we're actually in England, I can't wait.”

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV

The tipping ace believes there are some interesting angles worth exploring at the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup at Ascot where two of his three recommended bets run

View 2 Images Steve Jones with his picks for Saturday

Put on your Dancing shoes for the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup. Ascot’s annual team event isn’t everyone’s cup of tea but it’s unique formula, that pits jockeys from across the world against each other, does open up some interesting angles.

‌



Horses ridden by the likes of Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle are sure to be popular in the betting, but the competition is sometimes lit up by a foreign rider.

‌



It could be Hong Kong-based Luke Ferraris this year. His first ride this year is on DANCING IN PARIS (2.10) and he looks to have a much better chance than his odds suggest in the Shergar Cup Stayers.

‌

Half Price Tickets to York Races Ladies Day READ MORE :

He ran a sound race behind smart prospect Al Azd at Ascot a couple of weeks ago considering the 1m4f trip is too short for him these days.

This 2m distance suits him better as he showed when runner-up in last year’s Northumberland Plate. He was also an excellent fourth behind subsequent Group 2 winner Santorini Star at York.

The handicapper has started to cut him some slack and he could be about to take advantage. Have 1pt each-way at 16-1. A few bookies are paying out on four places.

‌



The Gosdens have struggled to find the key to MAY ANGEL (3.20) but Ascot’s stiff 6f of the Shergar Cup Sprint might suit him perfectly. He has done most of his racing over 7f and he was always going to find things happening a bit quickly when dropped to 5f for the Palace Of Holyroodhouse Stakes at Royal Ascot.

View 2 Images Luke Ferraris: makes Shergar Cup debut

Newmarket’s sharper 6f wasn’t ideal in a hot handicap for three-year-olds at the July Meeting but he was only beaten less than three lengths despite his jockey taking it easy when it was clear he wasn’t going to win.

‌



Everything could be about to come together under experienced French rider Christophe Lemaire. Have 1pt each-way at 14-1. Several firms are offering four places.

Racing returns to Haydock following the course’s drainage issues. Top filly Fallen Angel is the star attraction in the Irish Stallion Farms Dick Hern Stakes but she might be worth taking on with PACIFIC MISSION (3.00).

She was runner-up in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf and she has had valid excuses for her two below-par runs this season. Have 1pt each-way at 9-1.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances

Barcelona have seen an opening bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodi turned down on Friday - but the La Liga giants are expected to return as they close in on the World Cup winner

View 3 Images Barcelona have launched an opening offer for Man City midfielder Rodri

Enzo Maresca has earmarked Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez as his top option to replace Rodri this summer.

‌



Barcelona have seen an opening offer of £38.5million rejected out of hand by City, who want closer to £60m. However, with just one year remaining on his contract and coming off a serious knee injury, City are open to selling at the right price.

‌



And Maresca, who is going into his first season as Pep Guardiola ’s replacement, sees Fernandez as the perfect replacement for the World Cup Golden Ball winner.

‌



The Italian worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss and according to the Independent, City are already exploring a possible move for the Argentinian.

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Fernandez is yet to report for Chelsea this summer after playing a huge role in Argentina’s rollercoaster ride to the World Cup final. The 25-year-old scored crucial goals in the knockout stages, including a screamer in the dramatic comeback against England in the semis.

However, he arguably cost his nation the chance of lifting a fourth world title after he inexplicably picked up two yellow cards in a matter of minutes.

‌



Chelsea paid £106m for the midfielder in 2023 and would want to make a profit on that, if they were to entertain an exit this summer.

Fernandez was sanctioned earlier this year after his desire to leave the London club was made public. Ex-boss Liam Rosenior was also forced to strip him of the vice captaincy before he was sacked for a disastrous run of results.

View 3 Images Chelsea want a reported £120m for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



New Blues boss Xabi Alonso hasn’t been able to train with the talismanic midfielder during his short tenure, but made it clear he wants him to remain at the club.

Speaking in July, Alonso said: "Yes we have spoken. But as you can imagine what we have spoken remains private,” and then when pressed if he wanted Fernandez to stay, he replied “yes”.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer, signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a whopping £116m. But with the exit of Bernardo Silva and the expected one of Rodri, more cover is required before the Premier League campaign begins.

‌



They have also been heavily linked with Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, who shone at the World Cup with Morocco, but his £86m valuation has led talks to an impasse.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

Speaking after City’s most recent pre-season friendly, Maresca admitted the club still had work to do in order to replace a number of senior players.

‌



“Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,” he told media at a press conference ahead of Wednesday’s clash with K-League All Stars.

“At the same time, we already know the squad lost some important players with experience with Bernardo, John [Stones], Nathan [Ake]…different players. For sure, there are things we need to do.

He added: “The reason I said there are things to do is because the transfer window is open and when it is open, anything can happen. It is August and then from September, when it’s closed, it is completely different.”

Sports.title: Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light
Sports.content:
Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light

Arsenal are preparing to confirm the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes after the soon-to-be former Newcastle captain completed his medical - and his shirt number seemingly been leaked

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal for £75million (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wear the No.39 shirt for Arsenal after academy star Louie Copley moved to a new number. Arsenal are preparing to confirm Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fixed fee of £75million to end the transfer saga.

‌



The 28-year-old said his goodbyes at Newcastle's training camp in Spain before completing his medical with Arsenal and signing a four-year contract. His signing still hasn't been announced, although the Gunners have dropped a clear hint on their website.

‌



Copley, who wore the No. 39 shirt in each of Arsenal's first two pre-season friendlies as well as in training sessions, has had his squad number changed to 38. It's a telltale sign that Guimaraes is now a Gunner and has taken his favourite number.

‌



The midfielder has worn 39 throughout his club career, including for former clubs Lyon and Athletico Paranaense. Guimaraes likes to wear the number because his dad's taxi cab in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil was #039.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

Whether the decision was Copley's is unknown, although he did wear No.38 when captaining Arsenal's under-21 side last season. Unfortunately for Copley, who's just 19 and highly regarded at London Colney, he suffered an injury just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute during the Gunners' 3-1 loss against Real Betis in a friendly on Wednesday.

‌



Mikel Arteta said post-match: "It doesn't look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either. Let's hope that tomorrow [Thursday] the news is better than we hope."

Guimaraes will become Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer, with the Gunners having also brought in Christos Tzolis for £34m and Illan Meslier on a free transfer. The Brazilian is expected to partner Declan Rice in midfield once the season gets going.

Who should Arsenal sign next? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Louie Copley's number has been changed on the Arsenal website

By leaving Newcastle, Guimaraes becomes the third key player to depart St James' Park this summer as well as manager Eddie Howe. New Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle said: "I met him quickly, but the decision was already made. It was a nice conversation.

"He's a fantastic player and a great human being. It's tough but for him now it's the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage. We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
