World.title: Paide and Flora both lose in UEFA Conference League qualifying first legs
World.content:
Estonia's representatives at the UEFA Conference League suffered defeats home and away on Thursday, as Paide Linnameeskond went down to Rapid Vienna (Austria) and Tallinna FC Flora lost 2-0 away to Inter Club d'Escaldes (Andorra).

The UEFA Conference League is the third tier of European club competition, and Thursday's games were the first leg of round three of qualifying, with a berth in the playoffs awaiting the aggregate winners.

Paide 1, Rapid Vienna 4

Paide Linnameeskond suffered a 4–1 home defeat against Rapid Vienna before 5,500 fans at the A. Le Coq Arena in Tallinn. The hosts kept the score at 1–1 before things began to unravel in the last 10 minutes.

This means they will go to Vienna for the second leg next week with a mountain to climb if they are to meet either Benfica or Hearts in the playoff round.

The 32-time Austrian champions Rapid started the match sharply and were awarded a penalty as early as the third minute, which Hungarian right-back Bendeguz Bolla duly slotted in.

The visitors kept up the pressure, keeping 75 percent of the possession in the first half, though such shots as they had were little threat to Paide's Gambian 'keeper Ebrima Jarju's goal, and some chances even began to emerge for the home side as well.

This manifested with a Paide equalizer in the 41st minute when a low corner made its way into Rapid's penalty area; a touch from striker Abdourahman Badamosi hit the crossbar before it fell to forward Daniel Luts, who fired it into the net from a few meters out.

However, Rapid got back in control of the tempo in the second half. In the 71st minute, Paide committed a poor misplaced pass near their own penalty area, though Jarju saved the resulting close-range effort. Two minutes later, it was Rapid's goalkeeper's turn to keep out a fierce shot at his near post from striker Modou Pa Sohna.

In the final 10 minutes, however, the visitors settled things once and for all with three unanswered goals. In the first of these, Jarju came off his line in time to cut out a through ball, but the ball unfortunately ricocheted to striker Moulaye Haidara, who calmly slotted it home. Just two minutes later, Bolla delivered a low cross from the right into the goalmouth, where winger Petter Dahl turned it into the net, and in the fourth minute of stoppage time, Haidara capped a fine attack to put the finishing touch on the match.

Benfica meanwhile put six past Hearts, while the latter responded with just the one goal, in their first leg of the same qualifying stage.

Tallinna FC FLora players. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Flora lose 2–0 away to Andorran champs

Meanwhile reigning Estonian champions FC Flora went down 2–0 away to Andorran league champions Inter Club d'Escaldes in the first leg of their third-round qualifier, for the same competition.

Despite being based in tiny Andorra, the hosts have picked up some notable victories in the Conference League competition in recent years. Three summers ago, they defeated Scottish Premiership club Hibernian at home in the second qualifying round of the Conference League. Then last season, they beat Romanian giants FCSB, and drew with Slovenian powerhouse Olimpija Ljubljana.

AVUI JUGA UN DELS NOSTRES!



UEFA Conference League

➡️ Tercera eliminatòria (anada)



Inter Club Escaldes - Flora Tallinn

19h

️ Nou Estadi de la FAF

Encamp pic.twitter.com/xapXCvX29D — Federació Andorrana de Futbol (@Fedandfut) August 6, 2026

Inter are reigning Andorran league champions, though they have only one Andorran player in their squad, who came on for the final 10 minutes on Thursday. The overwhelming majority of the squad are Spanish nationals, many of them products of the academies of major clubs. For example, Inter midfielder Juan Camara has appeared for Barcelona in a Champions League match, while Inter Club d'Escaldes 'keeper Javi Diaz has played for La Liga side Sevilla.

The first half of Thursday's match belonged entirely to the hosts: Forward Faysal Chouaib put Inter ahead as early as the fifth minute, with the Andorran champions retaining 75 percent of possession during the first half, registering 13 shots during that time to Flora's two, one of which was on target.

The visitors came out for the second half in much better shape, however, holding more possession and even creating some chances in front of the hosts' goal. One good opportunity fell to national team striker Rauno Sappinen, but he was not ready for the ball inside Inter's penalty area. However, it was Inter who doubled their lead, in the 62nd minute, thanks to a goal from winger Domi Berlanga. The hosts held on to that margin to the final whistle, taking that advantage into the second leg in Estonia next Thursday, August 13.

World.title: Estonian raspberries thrive as new methods help farms weather changes
World.content:
Estonian raspberry growers are reporting a strong season this year as farms turn to new growing methods to protect crops from increasingly unpredictable weather.

Recent years of volatile spring and summer weather have pushed growers to experiment with new ways of cultivating raspberries. This summer, those adaptations combined with favorable weather conditions have helped berry farms achieve a strong harvest.

At Tontoli Berry Farm in Põlva County, raspberries are now grown in outdoor pots instead of directly in the ground.

Owner Kardo Tamm said the plants are also set out later in spring, with early-season raspberry plants initially kept in greenhouse-like tunnels to shield them from spring frosts.

The later planting schedule has helped protect their plants from cold.

"This year's raspberry harvest has been good," Tamm said. "We haven't had heavy rains that damage the berries during harvesting, and the cold this spring didn't do too much damage."

At Joosepi Farm in Ahja, the first tunnel-grown raspberries ripened around Midsummer, while outdoor potted raspberry plants are now reaching peak production.

Owner Kaire Roositalu said their harvest is expected to continue through late August.

"We have a lot of raspberries," she said, calling this year's harvest good. She noted that the outdoor crop is only just getting started.

World.title: Careless waste handling attracts rodents to the city
World.content:
The Põhja‑Tallinn district government is collecting tips about rat and mouse activity through mid‑August to direct pest control efforts to the most affected areas. Experts say careless waste handling encourages rodent spread.

Kadri Karnau, communications specialist at the Tallinn Environment and Public Works Department, said the city does not gather centralized statistics on rodent numbers because they cannot be reliably assessed. Still, residents' observations are welcome because they help identify larger colonies.

Rodent control in the capital is divided by areas of responsibility, meaning homeowners' associations play an important role. "When a colony is discovered, the first step is to speak with the private property owner or the homeowners' association, which is responsible for rodent control. The city and district government can only carry out control on areas they manage," Karnau said.

The Environment and Public Works Department uses rat poison placed in special plastic boxes. Karnau said districts do not conduct large‑scale preventive poisoning because it would pose a danger to pets, birds and people. Control is always targeted and based on specific nesting sites and movement paths.

Ettevõtmise eesmärk on leida üles kõige probleemsemad ja pahategelikud rotid. Autor/allikas: slyfox photography/Unsplash

Joosep Sarapuu, a zoologist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, said local control will not eliminate rodents from the city. "It is not possible in practice to achieve 100‑percent eradication of rats. When one colony disappears, the area becomes freely accessible to newcomers again," he said.

Rat control is complicated by their biological behavior. They exhibit neophobia, meaning fear of new objects. When a plastic box with poison or a trap appears, rodents need time before they dare to approach it.

A common belief that colonies send their weakest members to test poison is not entirely accurate, Sarapuu said. "Dominant individuals do not check new things because they have established routes and a stable food supply. Lower‑ranking members are forced to look for new feeding sites and movement paths. That is why they are the first to encounter poison and traps," he said.

Joosep Sarapuu. Source: ERR

How can people keep rodents away from their homes? Sarapuu said summer is a good time to check a home's rodent‑proofing because pests try to enter houses when the weather gets cold. "You should find small gaps and openings where rats and mice can get inside and seal them carefully. Second, you must check food waste to make sure it is not easily accessible. In that case, rodents are likely to be fewer or not present at all," he said.

Karnau also said a tidy neighborhood is the best way to keep rodents away. "Trash rooms and waste containers must be kept in good condition and closed to prevent food waste from spreading into the surroundings. It is also wise to avoid feeding birds and squirrels and to keep the areas under bird feeders clean because fallen food attracts rodents," she said.

World.title: Expert: Talk of a direct Russian attack is extremely foolish
World.content:
Claims by anonymous American intelligence sources that a possible limited Russian attack against NATO may happen in the coming years are exaggerated speculation, said security expert Rainer Saks, former secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2015-2020) and the Foreign Intellegence Service (2011-2015).

ERR: A U.S. intelligence assessment has been published by The Wall Street Journal, stating that Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whose invasion of Ukraine has stalled, could test NATO in the coming years by attacking one of the alliance's member states. The report mentions both cyberattacks and a limited ground incursion. What should we make of all this?

Rainer Saks: First of all, this is another classic case where anonymous sources have said something, fragments have been written down, but official comments are either unavailable or refused. It is a very broad and diffuse text.

As for these general assessments that Russia "could do something," there is no significant indication behind them that Russia is actually planning to do so. It is a hypothetical assessment that Russia could do this, that or the other. As long as Russia is not planning such actions, publishing assessments like this in the current context actually works very much in Russia's favor. Even the suggested time frame, from this autumn until 2029, is completely absurd.

Russia is certainly not making plans like that.

It is difficult to judge whether this was leaked by the U.S. government or is the initiative of an individual intelligence official. We will not speculate about that, but this is speculation rather than a report based on a concrete intelligence assessment.

The proposed actions — from cyberattacks to a limited military incursion — essentially cover the entire range of scenarios that could theoretically be considered. Therefore, I would not take this at present as a serious warning requiring the rapid implementation of countermeasures.

For example, Russia has been carrying out cyberattacks against NATO member states continuously since at least 2005–2006.

At the same time, NATO countries' responses have so far not been appropriate, because before the invasion of Ukraine, several European countries sought to engage Russia and develop energy cooperation instead. Examples of the kind of situation described in the intelligence report can also be found 15 to 20 years ago, so there is nothing new in it.

At the moment, publishing such a report works more to Russia's advantage, because Russia itself has not directly threatened NATO countries with any military action. Instead, a context is now being created that allows it to manipulate information even more than it has done so far.

In that sense, I think the text published by The Wall Street Journal is extremely foolish.

The article also points to indications that Russia is already testing NATO's response, for example, drones and missiles have fallen on the territory of Romania and Poland. This is presented as one indication that perhaps something is underway.

At the same time, those very countries have themselves said that they do not regard this as deliberate Russian action, but rather as accidental or technical incidents. I cannot say whether the official comments differ drastically from what is actually happening.

This is, of course, a problem because while active warfare is taking place in Ukraine, the possibility of, for example, Ukrainian drones ending up in allied territory or being shot down there is indeed an elevated risk.

There are only two main scenarios under which Russia would begin testing NATO's unity.

The first is that NATO has completely fallen apart internally. Although NATO's unity has suffered in several respects recently, there is no full political unity and there are sharp disagreements between different member states, it cannot be said that there is no unity at all. I would not yet go so far as to claim that NATO's collective defense has therefore been called into question.

The domestic political problems of member states and NATO's internal weakening are, in fact, the most likely scenario that could lead to a military confrontation between Russia and a NATO member state. At the moment, however, that process is clearly not advancing rapidly.

The second theoretical possibility is that if Russia truly decides to attack NATO militarily, it would first have to reorganize its forces. For such an attack — or even a test — to be genuinely supported, Russia would most likely have to carry out a mobilization. To some extent, that is theoretically possible after the State Duma elections, because the forces fighting against Ukraine have been unable to achieve success, and according to the Russian General Staff's calculations, there are too few troops.

In a situation where a full-scale war is still being fought in Ukraine, launching a new war against an even stronger opponent would, in my view, require Russia to declare martial law and carry out full-scale mobilization. That is something without which I do not believe Russia would proceed with very aggressive plans.

The article repeatedly refers to the fact that the Americans are running low on missile stockpiles because of operations in the Middle East and donations to Ukraine. Could it instead be that this article and the intelligence assessment are aimed at a domestic U.S. audience, to remind people of the need to replenish weapons stockpiles quickly?

That may indeed be the case. However, there is one important nuance here: the issue is not that the United States lacks certain types of missiles in its stockpiles, primarily air defense missiles and Tomahawk-type long-range strike weapons, of which too many have been expended against Iran. It is natural for stockpiles to decline during active military operations, but production is reportedly not keeping pace with what is needed. That is an embarrassing situation — what is the point of launching military operations if you cannot simultaneously replenish your stocks?

What is being overlooked, however, is that Russia has exactly the same problem, only even more severe. It also lacks sufficient air defense capabilities, as demonstrated by the success of Ukraine's long-range strikes. For example, this morning yet another large Wildberries warehouse, deep in the Urals some 1,800 kilometers from Ukraine, was set on fire.

Russia is in exactly the same position of weakness. Its entire missile capability is focused on Ukraine, and it is unable to carry out large-scale missile strikes on a daily basis. The war has lasted four years and has significantly exhausted Russia.

Of course, we can talk about hybrid attacks, but the conditions for Russia to launch a military incursion into NATO territory or start a military conflict with NATO are in no way favorable for Russia at present.

Why do you think intelligence assessments claiming that Russia is about to start testing NATO keep being published, when in reality they do not correspond to the facts?

I cannot answer that question. It is probably influenced by many different factors, ranging from incompetence and foolishness to domestic political objectives.

There is, of course, genuine reason to be concerned about the overall situation. There is nothing good about it. A major war is underway, and the governments of Europe and the United States have been unable to bring it to an end. That is indeed a very serious problem. Supporting Ukraine has also not been as successful as it should have been — a great deal has been done, but not enough.

A separate question is why European leaders have been unable to pull themselves together. Four years after the start of the full-scale war, they are still unable to produce enough of the military equipment that is needed. That is a very bad sign. In that sense, it is understandable that many people are seriously concerned about the situation and are trying to warn of possible negative developments.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy
World.content:
Marking National Handloom Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister

on Thursday paid tribute to the State's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage and emphasising their role in carrying forward traditions that have been passed down through generations.

Addressing a gathering in Lucknow after presenting the Sant Kabir State-Level Handloom Awards, the Chief Minister congratulated artisans across the State and linked the occasion to India's freedom movement.

"Today is National Handloom Day. I congratulate all the artisans across the state on Handloom Day. It was on this very day, August 7, 1905, that India's freedom struggle received a new direction," Adityanath said.

He recalled that August 7 commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement, which encouraged Indians to embrace indigenous products and reject foreign goods during the freedom struggle. According to the Chief Minister, the movement not only strengthened the spirit of self-reliance but also boosted confidence in India's traditional industries, particularly handloom weaving.

The Chief Minister said the handloom sector is more than an economic activity.





It represents India's identity, craftsmanship and cultural continuity. He stated that every handwoven fabric carries the story of the artisan behind it and reflects centuries of skill, patience and creativity.

Uttar Pradesh is home to several renowned handloom traditions, including the Banarasi silk saree, Chikankari embroidery of Lucknow, Bhadohi carpets and handwoven textiles from Mau, Tanda and Mubarakpur.

These crafts provide livelihoods to thousands of weaving families and contribute significantly to the state's economy and exports.

Adityanath said recognising artisans through state-level awards is an effort to encourage excellence while inspiring younger generations to preserve traditional crafts. He added that supporting weavers through government initiatives, better market access and modern technology is a priority.

World.title: Watch: Delhi-NCR drowns in rain chaos; 7 videos show waterlogging, gridlock
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Heavy rainfall lashed several parts of Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) on Friday, leading to widespread waterlogging, traffic congestion and disruptions to vehicular movement during peak hours.

The IMD issued a red alert, forecasting moderate rain at many places and heavy rain at isolated locations accompanied by moderate thunderstorms and lightning over the next few hours. According to the weather office, Safdarjung recorded 59.2 mm of rainfall till 8.30am, while Lodhi Road received 60.4 mm, Ridge 57 mm, Ayanagar 26.2 mm and Palam 16.9 mm.

The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall over Delhi till August 10.

Heavy waterlogging reported

Heavy waterlogging was reported near Badarpur Border Metro Station, where rainwater entered the subway, making it difficult for commuters to pass through. Several low-lying roads in the area were submerged, forcing vehicles to move cautiously.

Traffic hit across key stretches

The downpour led to long traffic snarls on major roads.

One of the worst-hit stretches was the Barapullah Flyover, where a long queue of vehicles stretched across multiple lanes.





Visuals show cars, buses, auto-rickshaws and two-wheelers crawling in dense traffic, with headlights and brake lights illuminating the rain-soaked carriageway. Traffic remained gridlocked in both directions as rain slowed movement during the evening rush hour.

World.title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a âstrong foundation for progression within the groupâ.

The group has tried to do multiple things â make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.

AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay â meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours.

This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.

Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.





The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west â unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers â means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.

Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.

While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.

Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors.

The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.

âNew career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,â said an official.

Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.

âAs AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India.

Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,â said teh official.

Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as âthe primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades.

This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.â

Following command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. âWith 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,â the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.

World.title: India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
World.content:
BENGALURU: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure, a move expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations.

âThe Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach, developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is designed exclusively for helicopters. The procedure was validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA),â HAL said Friday.

The new approach, it added, enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation, allowing them to safely negotiate terrain and urban obstacles while operating in adverse weather conditions.

According to HAL, the procedure cuts the approach time to HAL Airport from around 12 minutes to about 4 minutes.

âThe operationalisation of Indiaâs first RNP CAT H helicopter approach is a significant milestone for the countryâs aviation ecosystem. This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented at airports across the country,â HAL chairman and managing director Ravi K said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Besides improving safety, the system is expected to enhance operational efficiency and airspace capacity by allowing smoother integration of helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft movements. It also reduces the noise footprint over urban areas by enabling more precise flight paths.

The faster approach routes are expected to benefit time-critical operations such as air ambulance services and search-and-rescue missions. HAL Airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the countryâs busiest helicopter hubs. The introduction of the RNP CAT H procedure addresses a long-standing gap in Indiaâs aviation infrastructure and could serve as a model for similar helicopter navigation procedures at other airports.

World.title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest?" the

remarked on Friday while refusing to entertain

(TMC) MP

's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in connection with a hate speech case.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

"The requirement as per the police's notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency.

Last time I went there two things happened. First there were threats that eggs will be thrown etc. and second time eggs were actually thrown," he submitted.

The bench, however, was unconvinced and orally observed, "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs?

"When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all," it added, according to news agency PTI.





With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition, following which it was dismissed as withdrawn.

The plea challenged a July 21 order of the Calcutta High Court, which had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action until October 5 in the hate speech case, while directing her to cooperate with the investigation.

World.title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
World.content:
Astrobase unveils India's first privately-built 800kN full-flow staged combustion rocket engine 'Everest', aiming for reusable launch systems and domestic launch infrastructure.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Space start-up Astrobase Space Technologies Friday unveiled what it described as Indiaâs first privately built â800kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) liquid oxygen-methane rocket engine, named âEverestââ, as it seeks to develop reusable launch systems and expand domestic launch infrastructure.The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations. The next major milestone for the programme will be a full-engine hot-fire test, followed by vehicle integration and orbital launch development.According to the company: âEverest uses the full-flow staged combustion cycle, one of the most complex rocket engine architectures, and is powered by liquid oxygen and methane. The engine has been designed for reusability and offers 800 kN of thrust, a specific impulse of around 340 seconds and a throttle range of 50% to 110%.âThe company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational, with the capability to hot-fire about one engine every week. It aims to test around 20 engines before attempting its first orbital mission.Its first phase of expansion is intended to support about 100 tonnes of annual launch capacity, with a longer-term goal of exceeding 1,000 tonnes through a higher launch cadence.It also said it was âworking towards a launch-on-demand capability that could enable a dedicated mission within 15 days of an urgent national requirement. These targets are yet to be demonstratedâ.Astrobase co-founder Neeraj Khandelwal said the engine was intended to establish an industrial capability rather than serve only as a technology demonstrator, adding that India would require indigenous high-thrust propulsion systems as satellite launches increase globally.IN-SPACe director (technical) Rajeev Jyoti said Astrobase was among the recipients of IN-SPACeâs Technology Adoption Fund, which is supporting development of the 800 kN engine. He said the programme, as it progresses through development and testing, could contribute to Indiaâs launch capability and create new opportunities in the global space economy.Founded in 2024, Astrobase is developing propulsion systems, test infrastructure and reusable launch technologies from its Bengaluru base.

World.title: 'Govt stealing money, destroying lives': Rahul Gandhi vows campaign against E20
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

on Friday said Congress will soon take up the issue of the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel programme.

In a social media post on X, Rahul shared a video and accused the government of "stealing directly out of people's pockets".

"This E20 issue is a very serious matter. Usually, we say, 'Daal mein kuch kaala hai.' But here, the whole daal is black," the Congress leader said.

"Brothers and sisters, this is a matter of priorities. In any campaign, we have to decide the order in which issues are taken up. The problem right now is that there is so much corruption that there is a long list of issues we have to prioritise. But don't worry. We will take up the E20 issue in a big way because it is damaging people's cars and scooters and their lives and is, quite literally, stealing money directly out of their pockets," he added.

The remarks came days after Congress alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol had increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming motorists were paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country had been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".

Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised.





"On the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately Rs 88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel," he wrote in a post on X.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers.

"E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. If any segment has benefited the most from E20, it is the ethanol producers," Ramesh said.

However, the Centre has maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil and supports farmers by creating demand.

World.title: Evening news wrap: CBI chargesheet alleges NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG, MEA rejects US criticism of of FCRA Bill & more
World.content:
CBI chargesheet alleges NTA experts leaked NEET-UG 2026 papers for cash in a multi-state conspiracy .

. MEA rejected US criticism of FCRA Bill as an internal matter for Parliament to decide.

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed a mutual defence pact; India says it is 'closely following' it.

PM Modi advised 45 NDA MPs to avoid the 'Lutyens web' and not carry House anxiety outside.

Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi sparked buzz over a possible BJP-SAD reunion ahead of Punjab polls.

Here are the top 5 stories of the day

CBI chargesheet exposes NTA experts' role in NEET-UG paper leak for money

The CBI has chargesheeted 13 accused, including three NTA subject experts, for allegedly leaking NEET-UG 2026 question papers in a well-coordinated multi-state conspiracy in exchange for large sums of money.

The agency said its investigation uncovered a supply chain linking the experts to middlemen and coaching operators who distributed the leaked papers through messaging apps days before the exam.

India rejects US lawmaker's FCRA criticism, says Parliament will decide

India rejected criticism by a US lawmaker over the proposed FCRA amendments, saying the issue is an internal matter on which Parliament will take a decision. The remarks came after US Congressman Riley Moore called the bill "a clear attack against Christians" and warned it could affect bilateral ties.

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan & Turkey sign 'Mecca' pact for mutual defence; India reacts

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed a trilateral defence agreement on Friday, stating that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all. India's MEA said it is "closely following" the development.

PM Modi tells NDA MPs: Avoid 'Lutyens web', stay calm in Parliament

PM Modi met 45 newly elected and first-time NDA MPs at a breakfast meeting on Friday, advising them to "not carry the anxiety from inside the House to outside" and avoid the "web of Lutyens' Delhi."

He also told them to maintain dignity, avoid shouting in anger, and engage actively on social media.

Badal-Modi meeting reignites talk of BJP-SAD reunion in Punjab

SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal met PM Modi in Parliament on Friday, sparking fresh buzz over a possible BJP-SAD reunion ahead of the Punjab assembly elections due early next year. The two parties, allies for over two decades, parted ways in 2020 over the Centre's three farm laws.

World.title: Tiruchi, Thanjavur and Pullambadi ITIs among those identified for upgradation under PM SETU scheme
World.content:
The State government has identified six clusters of government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Tamil Nadu for being upgraded under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme.

This was disclosed by Jayant Chaudhary, Union Minister for State (Independent charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, in the Lok Sabha recently in response to a query raised by Perambalur MP K. N. Arun Nehru on the upgradation of ITIs in his constituency.

The scheme envisages the upgradation of 1,000 government ITIs in the country in a hub and spoke model. The upgraded ITIs would get smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content and new courses aligned to industry needs.

The Government ITIs in Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Hosur, Madurai, Thoothukudi and Ambattur are the identified hubs. Government ITIs in Thanjavur, Pudukottai, Pullambadi (ITI for women) and Viralimalai would come under the Tiruchi hub.

The government ITIs in Dharapuram, Gobichettipalayam, Coimbatore (Women) and Erode would come under the Coimbatore hub, while the Madurai Hub will have the Dindigul, Theni, Karaikudi and Paramakudi government ITIs as its spokes.

The Hosur Government ITI will have as its spokes the Salem, Dharmapuri, Salem (women) and Mettur Dam ITIs. The Tirunelveli, Tiruchendur, Nagercoil and Virudhunagar ITIs will form the spokes of the Thoothukudi ITI hub, while the Chengalpattu, Perumbakkam, Vellore and Ranipet ITIs will come under the Ambattur hub.

The selection of ITIs under the PM-SET scheme is done by the respective Stage governments in consultation with industry and local industrial potential, the Minister said.

Improving the quality of training in the ITIs, modernising the infrastructure and equipment as per industry standards, introducing industry-aligned long-term and short-term courses, especially in new and emerging sectors, and strengthening industry linkage for demand-driven skilling were among the key objectives of the scheme.

World.title: Former Panchayat president shot dead in Mudarangadi
World.content:
In second of such incidents in Udupi district in a week, contractor and former president of Mudarangadi Gram Panchayat David D’Souza was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne assailants in Pilar of Mudarangadi Gram Panchayat on Friday.

On July 31, businessman Richard Mascarenhas was allegedly shot dead by one Derrick Crasta in Kundapur town.

A CCTV footage of the incident being circulated on social media showed that one of the assailants approached D’Souza from behind when the latter was about to get into the driving seat of his car in front of St. Francis Xavier Church in Pilar. The assailant hit D’Souza and he collapsed. Soon after he shot at D’souza from a close range, the assailant veiled the weapon to threaten people in the area. The assailant was seen getting onto his accomplice’s motorcycle and fleeing from the scene. Injured D’Souza was taken to a nearby hospital, where the doctors declared him brought dead. The reason for the murder was not known.

Police personnel from the jurisdictional Shirva police station and the neighbouring Padubidri police station rushed to spot. Scene Of Crime and Dog squad personnel were also requisitioned. Efforts were being made to trace the assailants, the police said.

World.title: Bombay HC to hear Gadkari's plea against Meta and others over ethanol-linked deepfake posts on Aug. 5
World.content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) said it would hear on August 5 Union Minister Nitin Gadkari’s suit against Meta, X, Google, and unknown persons over allegedly defamatory deepfake content circulated on social media, falsely linking him to the Centre’s Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP).

The Bench of Justice Arif Doctor directed the Union Minister’s advocate Sandeep S. Ladda to serve copies of the civil suit to all respondents and adjourned the matter.

Mr. Gadkari has sought damages of ₹11 crore, alleging that the viral content has tarnished his reputation.

The single-judge Bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja on Monday (July 27) noted the background of the case and observed that the EBP was introduced in 2003 as a national policy, aiming to blend ethanol with petrol in phases. Between 2025 and 2026, the government achieved 20% blending (E20). The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas oversees the policy and has issued press releases and clarifications on its implementation.

Mr. Gadkari, who has been the Union Minister of Road Transport since 2014, said he has no role in the E20 policy. He alleged that unknown users created and circulated AI-generated deepfake and defamatory content, falsely portraying him as responsible for the EBP.

The plea identifies 24 social media posts that allegedly defame Mr. Gadkari and link him to the E20 controversy. The Union Minister urged the court to order the removal of the posts and sought ₹11 crore in damages for the alleged harm caused to his reputation.

World.title: Weak Southwest monsoon hits farmers in Nilgiris
World.content:
A lack of rainfall in The Nilgiris has begun severely affecting farmers in the district.

According to officials, a rainfall deficit of anywhere between 30% and 70% has been recorded in regions across the Nilgiris, with an average deficit of 50%. Speaking to The Hindu, P. Raja, scientist and head of the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Horticulture Research Station in the Nilgiris, said that the deficit in rainfall was alarming. The Horticulture Department stated that the Nilgiris has received only 283 millimetres of rain in 2026, as opposed to the average of 874 millimetres it receives every year — a 47% decrease. The rainfall deficit is even more stark when compared with 2025, when the district received 1,038 millimetres of rain during the Southwest monsoon.

“In other deficit years, the rainfall deficit during the Southwest monsoon rarely exceeded 10%. The rains in the Nilgiris usually begin around June 10 and continue till August 20. However, this year, there were rains for a week in June, and there have been no rains since,” Dr. Raja said.

El Niño effect

Dr. Raja said that the very strong effects of the El Niño climate pattern could potentially be causing a deficit in rainfall in the district. He said that the KVK in the Nilgiris was advising farmers on crop selection and other methods to mitigate the economic impacts of the lack of rainfall on their farms. As the Nilgiris and other districts in the Western Ghats receive the majority of their annual rainfall during the Southwest monsoon, experts believe that the lack of rainfall could lead to a drought this year.

R. Hariharan, a farmer from Ketti Palada in the Nilgiris, said that they had already begun witnessing the impacts of the lack of rain, with many farms suffering losses due to a shortage of rainfall. “We have been witnessing farms growing garlic and other English vegetables being particularly impacted,” he said. Other affected areas include Gudalur, where the lack of rains has resulted in a delay in the paddy sowing season.

Crop advisory

The KVK in the Nilgiris is advising farmers on crop selection, urging them not to use hybrid seeds to cultivate carrots, garlic, and beetroot. Instead, farmers have been advised to use non-hybrid seed varieties, which are known to be more resilient. They can also opt to grow potatoes, as well as medicinal and aromatic herbs, this year.

Joint Director of Horticulture (Nilgiris district) P. Maragathamani said that the government had issued advisories to farmers on steps they could take to mitigate the effects of a lack of water available for farming. She said that the Horticulture Department would hold village-level meetings in affected areas with local farmers and guide them on measures they could take to mitigate the effects.

“We are also promoting sprinkler irrigation and organic farming of tea by increasing the use of organic manure, and providing subsidies to farmers to construct rainwater harvesting structures to minimise water usage and maximise water saving,” said Ms. Maragathamani. She added that farmers were being advised to adopt mulching, either using biodegradable plastic or stubble mulching in their fields for all crops.

World.title: Founder president of Shri Saibhakt Laxmibai Shinde Trust’s Shailaja 'Maa' Shinde–Gaikwad Patil passes away
World.content:
Shailaja “Maa” Shinde–Gaikwad Patil (80), the founder president of Shri Saibhakt Laxmibai Shinde Trust, passed away peacefully due to age-related ailments on Friday, August 1, 2026, at 7:15 p.m.

Her demise has cast a profound sense of grief over the Shinde–Gaikwad Patil family and the global Sai devotee community.

World.title: U.S. accounts for 67% of India’s LPG imports, Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri
World.content:
The U.S. now accounts for about 67% of India’s liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) imports, according to Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Mr. Hardeep Singh Puri .

Addressing the CII International Energy Conference, he said the shift follows an earlier government decision to source roughly 10% of India’s LPG requirements from the U.S. as part of a broader effort to diversify energy supplies.

“Some of us wondered would we need the 10% (from U.S.) when we have suppliers nearby [in the Gulf]. Today, I am happy to inform that U.S. accounts for about 67% of our LPG imports,” he said.

Before the conflict broke out in West Asia, India imported nearly 60% of its requirement of the bottled hydrocarbon gas, of which approximately 90% came via the Strait of Hormuz.

In his address, Mr. Puri elaborated that at the peak of crisis, India’s oil marketing companies (OMCs) ramped up their cumulative daily production of LPG from 34,000 metric tonnes to 55,000 metric tonnes, which helped the country offset the impact of lower imports.

‘No proposal to levy charges on LPG’

Speaking to reporters outside, Mr. Puri refuted news reports about the government seeking to impose an additional charge on LPG and natural gas to fund a strategic fuel reserve. “I am not aware of any such proposal,” he added.

World.title: Two arrested for robbing elderly woman
World.content:
The Konaje police on Friday, arrested two men on charges of robbing an elderly woman of a gold chain after assaulting her in their limits on August 3 and recovered the robbed item.

Police gave the names of the accused as Bala Subramanya, 49, resident of Matadakani-Urva and Shyam Kumar, 33, an autorickshaw owner and native of Thokkottu and currently residing near Bokkapatna Church, both in Mangaluru.

Bala Subramanya faces extortion cases in Bajpe, Mulki, Mangaluru East, Mangaluru North and Mangaluru Rural police stations.

Police said a 76 year-old woman noticed someone knocking on her door on August 3 and upon opening saw two unidentified persons asking for a rented house. Soon, they entered the house, threw her on the floor, assaulted her and robbed her of a gold chain and a bangle worth ₹3 lakh.

Konaje police who had registered cases of criminal tresspass and robbery, arrested the accused at Maroli based on specific information.

The City Police have said it is advisable to take safety measures, such as, opening doors carefully after verifying the visitor and installing CCTV cameras in the premises etc.

World.title: Residents of hill villages in Megamalai stage protest against eviction
World.content:
Thousands of people, mostly residents of hill villages in Megamalai region in Theni district, on Friday staged a protest at the Theni Collectorate. They protested against the eviction notices issued to them.

The protesters, led by CPI (M) State Secretary P. Shanmugam, urged the authorities not to evict the residents of the hill villages and urged the State government to file a revision petition in the Supreme Court and get back the rights to access for the people of the Megamalai region.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Shanmugam urged the State government not to evict the residents of the hill villages. He said as per the Forest Rights Act, land titles must be granted to the forest-dwelling residents and they should not be evicted from the forest lands. A petition was submitted to Theni Collector in this regard.

He said the Collector had informed them that a special meeting would be convened with all the stakeholders and the officials from various departments to address the issue. The protest was supported by various political parties and traffic along the Collectorate had to be diverted due to the massive gathering.

Earlier, the Forest Department issued notices to the residents of hill villages in Megamalai region. The residents of the villages have been living there for over 50 years. Agriculture was the main source of livelihood for these people.

The area was declared a part of Srivilliputhur- Megamalai Tiger Reserve. Following this, the Forest Department imposed various restrictions on the residents and also initiated measures to evict them from the land.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Shield of peace’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes.

Tarar said the agreement was aimed at strengthening defence cooperation and served as a form of deterrence rather than aggression. The minister further said Pakistan’s capabilities had been demonstrated during last year’s conflict with India and claimed that the country had since played a role in promoting regional peace.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

The regional conflagration has rained missile fire onto Gulf oil exporters, with Iran targeting Gulf countries in retaliation for attacks carried out against it using US military bases in the region.

The deal also comes as a 2022 truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has broken down.

After the two sides traded fire for the first time in years last month, Houthis declared a maritime blockade against the kingdom, threatening access to its ports, and has claimed to have attacked Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

Pakistan had condemned the Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”.

As the conflict expanded onto new fronts, Saudi Arabia last week unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

Saudi crown prince meets PM Shehbaz, Erdogan

Crown Prince Salman held separate meetings with PM Shehbaz and President Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace earlier in the day.

DPM Dar, CDF Munir and Asif were also present in the meeting with PM Shehbaz, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Meanwhile, Erdogan’s office confirmed on X that he also held a meeting with Crown Prince Salman.

PM Shehbaz arrived in Saudi Arabia on a three-day visit on Thursday, while the Turkish president undertook a one-day visit today, Anadolu Agency reported.

Erdogan landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, from where he departed for Makkah by road, the Turkish news outlet reported.

PM Shehbaz had landed in Jeddah on Thursday. CDF Munir later joined the Pakistani delegation, which also included Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi.

On Friday morning, the delegation visited the Holy Kaaba and performed Umrah, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz is also expected to visit Masjid-i-Nabvi (PBUH) in Madina.

According to an earlier statement by the FO, discussions between the two sides were to “focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relations as well as exchange of views on regional and international developments of mutual interests”.

The FO had noted that although the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, it carries “significance beyond the immediate crises and short-term considerations”.

It said the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

“The visit marks Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood,” the FO had emphasised.

Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Turkiye and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft.

In 2023, Riyadh agreed to buy Turkish drones in what Ankara called its largest defence export contract. In April this year, Saudi Arabia said it received a military force and fighter jets from Pakistan to boost the kingdom’s security.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held.

“High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked.

In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party.
